prior_passes.notes:
THIRD research pass (2026-07-31): START point still unresolved after a further round of leads that were NOT tried in passes 1-2. Result: no independently named, coordinate-able national-grid take-off/metering/dispatching station for the SEGAS feed has surfaced in any public source. Carrying forward the same 'New Damietta' broad-area placeholder as the best defensible anchor (per the task's own fallback instruction) rather than inventing a better-looking but unsupported point.

NEW LEADS RUN THIS PASS (none succeeded, all ruled out with reasons, so a future pass does not repeat them):

1) Spanish-language Union Fenosa Gas / Naturgy materials (elEconomista.es, unionfenosagas.com, revistapq.com, cnmv.es filings, elperiodicodelaenergia.com): rich on plant history, ownership, and the Damietta-Sagunto LNG shipping route, but none describe the domestic Egyptian gas-grid tie-in pipeline or name a station -- the Spanish corporate narrative is entirely downstream (export) side. EIB's own project page for 'DAMIETTA LNG PLANT' (eib.org/en/projects/pipelines/all/20010169, fetched directly, no login wall) covers only the plant and marine facilities, no pipeline scope. Hassan Allam Holding's project page (an EPC contractor) lists only civil/marine/storage-tank scope, no pipeline.

2) hydrocarbons-technology.com / offshore-technology.com / NS Energy / Global LNG Hub: all searched; hydrocarbons-technology.com now redirects into the same offshore-technology.com/GlobalData family as the already-cited seagas/ profile -- no separate, more-detailed project page exists publicly. None of these profiles name a supply-side station; all describe only the 140km/36-inch WDDM subsea feed line (Scarab/Saffron fields) as the plant's dedicated gas source, which is a different, already-known pipeline (not P6033).

3) Egypt Oil & Gas 2017 'Egypt Gas Transmission Infrastructure Map' (egyptoil-gas.com/maps/egypt-gas-transmission-infrastructure-map/, already used successfully for another row in this batch): downloaded and visually inspected at high zoom around Damietta. 'SEGAS LNG' has its own dedicated icon/line at the coast (a small Facilities-type icon at the river-mouth, consistent with the plant's real location) -- confirming the plant is treated as a distinct node on this map -- but the icon carries NO name/label of its own beyond 'SEGAS LNG', so it adds no new station name. A nearby label 'El horany' points to an unlabeled junction node on the same stretch of coast; investigated separately (see #6) and ruled out as a real facility name -- it is a village, not a gas station.

4) OSM/Overpass, widened to ~20-25km around New Damietta (man_made=pipeline+gas, gas_compressor nodes, valve nodes): re-attempted this pass but every public Overpass endpoint (overpass-api.de, overpass.kumi.systems, overpass.private.coffee) either rate-limited (HTTP 429) or timed out (HTTP 504/000) during this session -- could not get a fresh result. This is consistent with, not a reversal of, the second pass's own OSM/Overpass negative finding (no named take-off station tagged in the area).

5) Arabic press for 'محطة غاز دمياط الجديدة' / 'خط تغذية مصنع الإسالة' / 'جاسكو دمياط': surfaced only the SEGAS/Damietta-LNG plant's own history (Arabic Wikipedia, al-ain.com, masr360.net) and unrelated water/sewage infrastructure -- no gas take-off station name.

6) NEW THIS PASS -- three specific named GASCO trunk pipelines in the Damietta/Port Said corridor were tracked down via Arabic-language Marefa (المعرفة) pages and independently checked against the map, and ALL THREE were ruled out as NOT feeding SEGAS:
   - 'خط أنابيب الجميل-دمياط' (El Gamil-Damietta pipeline, 50km, 42-inch/4-inch conflicting spec in different sections, World Bank-financed, built 2016-2019 by Petrojet/Eni): its OWN technical routing section states it starts at the existing Port Fouad-Tina pipeline near Petrobel in El Gamil, Port Said, and terminates at existing valve room #13 on the 'Edko-Damietta pipeline' at Kafr El-Batikh, with its pressure-reduction station physically located INSIDE Burullus power station -- i.e. this project supplies Kafr El-Batikh/West Damietta-area POWER STATIONS, not the SEGAS LNG plant, despite the article's own generic intro line loosely saying it 'links to the gas liquefaction station in Damietta' (a Wikipedia-style oversimplification contradicted by the article's own routing detail). Confirmed also via a separate presidency.eg national-projects entry for 'ازدواج خط غاز الجميل-دمياط' (duplication of this same 42-inch/50km line, cost 1.089 billion EGP) -- again a power-station-feed project, not SEGAS.
   - 'خط أنابيب بورفؤاد-الطينة' (Port Fouad-Tina pipeline): runs Port Fouad (Port Said) NORTH-SOUTH into North Sinai (Tina Plain) -- a different corridor entirely, unrelated to Damietta.
   - 'خط أنابيب إدكو-دمياط' (Edko-Damietta pipeline): confirmed to exist as a named, GASCO-operated, government-owned trunk between Edko (Beheira governorate) and Damietta, but its own page is a stub with no route detail, no coordinates, and no named intermediate station -- it is the 'existing' trunk the El Gamil-Damietta project ties into at Kafr El-Batikh, but nothing publicly documents where/how it connects to SEGAS specifically.
   - Also found and ruled out: a fourth, separate 'Gamil-Fenussa' 42-inch/34km/397-million-EGP line explicitly built to feed WEST DAMIETTA POWER STATION (a different Damietta-area facility) -- not SEGAS, not a length/cost match for P6033.
   None of these four named trunks' specs (length, cost, purpose) match P6033's own sheet attributes.

7) SIGNIFICANT NEW CONTEXT (changes the framing for a future pass): GEM's own existing record for P6033 (checked for internal consistency only, per standing rule 1 never cited as a source) carries length 12km, diameter 42 inches, operator GASCO, START YEAR 2021, cost 340 million EGP. This means the pipeline is almost certainly NOT part of the plant's original ~2001-2004 construction (when Bechtel/Chiyoda-era EPC built the LNG train) but rather a GASCO project contemporaneous with Eni's Feb-2021-led restart of the plant after its 2012-2021 idle period -- fitting the second pass's corridor description of gas now increasingly sourced from the national grid/Nile Delta rather than only the dedicated WDDM subsea line. Targeted searches this pass for a GASCO/presidency.eg project entry matching '12km + 340 million EGP + 2021 + Damietta' specifically did NOT surface a matching named project (the four Damietta-corridor GASCO trunks found this pass are all different specs/dates/purposes, see #6). A GASCO annual report or investor/tender document for FY2020-2021 is the most promising untried source class for a future pass, since GASCO's own public website (gasco.com.eg -- Gas Grid, Compressor Stations, WDGC pages checked directly, WDGC is an unrelated Western Desert facility) has no project-level detail and its Compressor Stations page 404s.

Recommendation for a future pass: chase GASCO's Arabic-language annual report/investor disclosure PDFs for FY2020 or FY2021 (should list the '12km/42-inch/340M EGP' Damietta project by name if it is a formally named GASCO capital project), or a Ministry of Petroleum 'المشروعات القومية' 2021 project-completion press release naming the exact station -- rather than continuing general web search, which has now been exhausted across three passes and multiple languages.
